subject: dsm bug in smoothing parameter estimation

messages.author: 350dad0a615d36db
messages.subject: dsm bug in smoothing parameter estimation
parts:
Hi listfolk,

This is a warning for those using the DSM engine within Distance and the
dsm R package.

The latest mgcv update (1.8-23, release onto CRAN 2018-01-15) has
changed the behaviour of the gamma= option. Previously this was ignored
by the default fitting method in dsm, REML. Now the gamma argument is
passed when gamma is specified with REML or ML.

The previous behaviour of dsm was to set gamma=1.4 for models fitted
with GCV (as suggested in Kim & Gu, 2004). This was ignored when REML or
ML were used. The new behaviour is that "smoothing parameters are chosen
as if the sample size was n/gamma instead of n" (see
https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/mgcv/ChangeLog), giving rather
different estimates.

A new version of dsm is now on github and will appear on CRAN soon. It
will use gamma=1 for all methods. This will be incorporated into the
next version of Distance for Windows. In the meantime, setting gamma=1
explicitly in your models will get back to the "old" behaviour (sample
size =n) when method="REML" or method="ML". Those using method="GCV.Cp"
should set gamma=1.4 manually.

We continue to recommend folks use REML or ML for their models, as this
has strong theoretical basis for optimal smoothing at finite sample
sizes. But please ensure that gamma is set to 1 for REML/ML, unless you
have some specific reason to change it.

You can check previously run models by inspecting the model$call$gamma
and model$call$method elements, if your model is called "model". (A
gamma value of NULL means the default of 1 was used.)


Apologies this took a while for me to notice.


best,
--dave

--

References:

Kim, Y. and Gu, C. (2004), Smoothing spline Gaussian regression: more
scalable computation via efficient approximation. Journal of the Royal
Statistical Society: Series B (Statistical Methodology), 66: 337-356.
doi:10.1046/j.1369-7412.2003.05316.x
